sources.title: Mathematics textbooks for Classes VII, VIII and X

sources.usedFor: The school level the quantitative skills are pitched at, and the standard method each item uses.

skills.name: Number properties: factors, HCF and LCM
skills.description: Factors and multiples, highest common factor and least common multiple, and problems where events repeat on different cycles.

levels.AWARE: Knows what a factor, a multiple, the HCF and the LCM are, and which one a question about "sharing equally" or "happening together again" needs.
levels.GUIDED: Finds the HCF and LCM of two small numbers by listing multiples or by prime factors, following a worked example.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Finds the HCF and LCM of two or three numbers by prime factorisation and applies them to repeat-cycle word problems unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Spots when an answer is the HCF where the LCM was needed (or the product of the numbers), and checks the result divides or is divided by each number.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "computation of whole numbers … relationships between numbers"; UPSC GS Paper II "basic numeracy (numbers and their relations)"; NCERT Class X, Real Numbers (HCF and LCM by prime factorisation).
skills.expertCheck: Check the HCF/LCM scope is right for the aptitude block, and whether remainders and divisibility tests deserve their own skill.

skills.name: Arithmetic: order of operations, fractions and decimals
skills.description: The order of operations, adding and simplifying fractions, and multiplying decimals.

levels.AWARE: Knows that multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction, and that fractions need a common denominator to be added.
levels.GUIDED: Simplifies a short expression and adds two fractions with a written checklist of the steps.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Evaluates expressions, adds and simplifies fractions and multiplies decimals accurately without help.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Finds the step where a wrong result went astray — left-to-right evaluation, adding across fractions, a misplaced decimal point — and corrects it by estimation.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "computation of whole numbers, decimals, fractions"; UPSC GS Paper II "basic numeracy".
skills.expertCheck: Check whether BODMAS/order-of-operations is pitched at the right level for graduates, or should sit as a foundation-only skill.

skills.name: Percentages
skills.description: Percentage of a quantity, percentage change, reversing a percentage change, and successive changes.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a percentage is a part per hundred and that a percentage change is measured against the original value.
levels.GUIDED: Works out a percentage change and a successive change with a written method (multiplying factors).
levels.INDEPENDENT: Reverses a percentage change and compares two quantities in percentage terms unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Detects when the wrong base was used or successive changes were added, and checks answers by applying the change forwards.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "percentage"; NCERT Classes VII and VIII, comparing quantities.
skills.expertCheck: Check the "percentage of what" framing of each level is clear to a learner.

skills.name: Ratio and proportion
skills.description: Parts of a whole in a given ratio, direct and inverse proportion, and solving a proportion for an unknown.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a ratio compares parts, that the parts add to the whole, and the difference between direct and inverse proportion.
levels.GUIDED: Finds a whole or a part from a ratio and solves a proportion with a worked example alongside.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Decides whether a situation is direct or inverse proportion and solves it unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Recognises additive reasoning ("add the same amount") where multiplicative reasoning is needed, and checks that the ratio still holds.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "ratio and proportion"; NCERT Class VII, comparing quantities (ratio and proportion).
skills.expertCheck: Check that inverse proportion (workers and days) belongs here rather than only in time and work.

skills.name: Averages
skills.description: The mean of a list, combined (weighted) averages of two groups, and how the mean changes when a value is removed.

levels.AWARE: Knows that the mean is the total divided by the count and that it differs from the median.
levels.GUIDED: Finds a mean and a combined mean of two groups with a written total-then-divide method.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves average problems where the count changes or groups are combined, unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Spots an unweighted average of averages or a divide-by-the-old-count error, and checks with totals.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "averages".
skills.expertCheck: Check whether median and mode should be covered here or in data interpretation.

skills.name: Profit, loss and discount
skills.description: Profit and loss percentages on the cost price, successive discounts, and marking up then discounting.

levels.AWARE: Knows that profit and loss percentages are on the cost price and discounts are on the marked price.
levels.GUIDED: Works out profit percentage and a single or double discount with a checklist of which price is the base.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves mark-up-then-discount problems and successive discounts unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Detects profit computed on the selling price or percentages added across different bases, and verifies with actual prices.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "profit and loss, discount"; NCERT Class VIII, comparing quantities.
skills.expertCheck: Check the convention that profit percentage is on cost price is stated where a learner needs it.

skills.name: Simple and compound interest
skills.description: Simple interest over years and months, compound interest compounded annually, and the difference between interest and amount.

levels.AWARE: Knows the difference between simple and compound interest and between the interest and the amount.
levels.GUIDED: Computes simple interest and two-year compound interest from the formulas with a worked example.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves interest problems with months and with annual compounding unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Spots time left in months, compound interest treated as simple, or the amount given as the interest, and checks by year-by-year working.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "interest"; NCERT Class VIII, comparing quantities (compound interest).
skills.expertCheck: Check whether half-yearly compounding belongs in the ADVANCED band here.

skills.name: Time and work
skills.description: Combined work rates, finding one worker's time from a combined time, and pipes that fill and empty a tank.

levels.AWARE: Knows that work rates (work per day) add, not the days themselves.
levels.GUIDED: Finds a combined time from two individual times by adding rates, following a worked example.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves work problems including an emptying pipe unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Detects days added or averaged instead of rates, or an outflow counted as inflow, and checks by the work done in one day.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "time and work".
skills.expertCheck: Check the pipes-and-cisterns items sit well under this skill.

skills.name: Time, speed and distance
skills.description: Average speed over equal distances, converting km/h to m/s, and trains crossing a platform.

levels.AWARE: Knows that distance equals speed times time and that units must match.
levels.GUIDED: Converts between km/h and m/s and finds an average speed with total distance over total time, with the formula to hand.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves average-speed and train-length problems unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Spots an average of speeds taken as the average speed, a missing unit conversion or a missing length, and checks with total distance and time.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "time and distance".
skills.expertCheck: Check whether boats and streams should be added at the ADVANCED band.

skills.name: Mixtures and alligation
skills.description: Concentration of a mixture, the ratio for mixing two qualities to a target price, and repeated replacement.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a mixture's concentration is a weighted average of its parts.
levels.GUIDED: Finds a mixture's concentration and a mixing ratio using the alligation diagram with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves mixing-ratio and repeated-replacement problems unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Detects an unweighted average, a reversed alligation ratio or a linear treatment of replacement, and checks by computing the mixture back.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "mixture and alligation".
skills.expertCheck: Check the replacement items are not beyond the intended level.

skills.name: Linear equations and word problems
skills.description: Solving a linear equation in one unknown, the sum-and-difference problem, and age problems.

levels.AWARE: Knows that an equation stays balanced when the same operation is done to both sides.
levels.GUIDED: Solves a one-step or two-step linear equation and sets up a sum-and-difference problem with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Translates word problems (sums, differences, ages) into equations and solves them unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Finds a sign error on moving a term, an operation undone on only one term, or an answer to the wrong quantity, and checks by substituting back.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "basic algebra"; NCERT Class X, Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables.
skills.expertCheck: Check age problems are appropriate for the INTERMEDIATE and ADVANCED bands.

skills.name: Data interpretation
skills.description: Reading a small table of values by year: percentage change, the largest absolute change and the largest relative change.

levels.AWARE: Knows the difference between a value, an absolute change and a percentage change in a table.
levels.GUIDED: Reads values from a table and computes a percentage change with the formula to hand.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Compares absolute and relative changes across periods unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Spots a change divided by the later value, a level mistaken for a change, or absolute and relative growth confused, and rechecks from the table.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "data interpretation"; UPSC GS Paper II "data interpretation (charts, graphs, tables, data sufficiency etc.) — Class X level".
skills.expertCheck: Tables are written in text; check that is acceptable before charts exist in the item format. All figures are illustrative and describe no real organisation.

skills.name: Counting and basic probability
skills.description: Choosing a group (combinations), the probability of independent events together, and sums of two dice.

levels.AWARE: Knows that probability is favourable outcomes over equally likely outcomes, and when order matters in counting.
levels.GUIDED: Counts selections and computes a simple probability with a listed sample space.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves combination and independent-event problems unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Detects order counted when it does not matter, independent probabilities added, or outcomes treated as equally likely when they are not.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude (arithmetic reasoning); NCERT Class X, Probability.
skills.expertCheck: Check whether combinations are in scope for the aptitude block at this level.

skills.name: Number and letter series
skills.description: Finding the rule of a number or letter series and the next term.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a series follows a rule — a difference, a ratio, a pattern in the differences — and that letters can be read as positions 1 to 26.
levels.GUIDED: Finds the next term of a constant-difference or constant-ratio series by writing the differences.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Finds rules with changing differences, mixed operations and letter positions unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Tests a proposed rule against every given term and notices when a repeated difference does not fit.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "number series, alphabetical series".
skills.expertCheck: Check every series has one clear rule and the answer is unambiguous.

skills.name: Coding and decoding
skills.description: Letter-shift codes in either direction and letter-to-number codes.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a code applies one rule to every letter and that the rule can be found from a worked example.
levels.GUIDED: Finds a shift from a coded example and applies it to a new word with an alphabet strip.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Decodes and encodes with forward, backward and number codes unaided, including wrap-around from Z to A.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Checks a decoded word letter by letter and catches a shift in the wrong direction or miscounted by one.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "coding and decoding".
skills.expertCheck: Check the words used are neutral and the wrap-around cases are fair.

skills.name: Family relationships
skills.description: Working out how two people are related from a chain of statements.

levels.AWARE: Knows the basic relation words and that each statement adds one link between two people.
levels.GUIDED: Draws a family tree from the statements and reads a relation from it with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Works out relations across two or three generations unaided, including the words "only" and "no sons".
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Notices a skipped generation or an assumed gender and redraws the tree to check.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "blood relations".
skills.expertCheck: Check the relation words and family structures are neutral and familiar across Indian regions and family types.

skills.name: Direction sense
skills.description: Tracking turns and walks to find a final direction and a straight-line distance.

levels.AWARE: Knows the eight compass directions and that left and right depend on which way a person faces.
levels.GUIDED: Traces a walk on a sketch and finds the final direction with a compass drawn.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Finds direction and straight-line distance after several turns unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Catches left and right taken from the reader's view, or the total path given as the distance, and redraws to check.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "direction sense".
skills.expertCheck: Check the distance items stay within the Pythagorean triples a learner can do without a calculator.

skills.name: Syllogisms
skills.description: Deciding which conclusions follow from statements about groups (all, some, no), using only the statements.

levels.AWARE: Knows what "all", "some" and "no" claim, and that a conclusion must follow from the statements alone.
levels.GUIDED: Tests a conclusion with a Venn diagram of the statements with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Decides which conclusions definitely follow from two statements unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Catches a conversed "all", an assumed "some are not", a link through an undistributed middle term, or outside knowledge used instead of the statements.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "syllogistic reasoning"; UPSC GS Paper II "logical reasoning and analytical ability".
skills.expertCheck: Check each item's answer under the convention that "some" means "at least one" and "all A are B" implies "some B are A" (existence assumed), and that this convention is stated to learners.

skills.name: Ordering and ranking
skills.description: Positions in a row or queue from both ends, and arranging people or objects from clues.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a position counted from one end and from the other end share the person being counted.
levels.GUIDED: Places people from clues on a numbered sketch with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Solves rank and arrangement problems from several clues unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Catches an off-by-one count or a flipped left/right or before/after, and checks every clue against the final order.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "arrangement", "ranking".
skills.expertCheck: Check the arrangement items have exactly one order that satisfies every clue.

skills.name: Analogies and classification
skills.description: Completing a word analogy by its relationship, and finding the odd one out of a group.

levels.AWARE: Knows that an analogy repeats a relationship (tool to use, worker to place) and that an odd-one-out has one clear shared category.
levels.GUIDED: States the relationship in the first pair as a sentence and tests each option against it.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Completes analogies and classifications unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Rejects options that share only a surface feature with the pair, and checks the chosen relationship fits both pairs.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, General Intelligence and Reasoning: "analogies", "classification".
skills.expertCheck: Check every item has one intended relationship and no second defensible answer.

skills.name: Vocabulary: synonyms and antonyms
skills.description: Choosing the word closest or opposite in meaning to a given word.

levels.AWARE: Knows what a synonym and an antonym are and that the question asks for one or the other.
levels.GUIDED: Chooses a synonym or antonym for common words, using the word in a sentence to test.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Chooses synonyms and antonyms for less common words unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Catches an antonym picked for a synonym (or the reverse) and a word chosen because it looks or sounds like the given one.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, English Comprehension: "synonyms", "antonyms".
skills.expertCheck: Check the words are at the right level and each has one clearly best option.

skills.name: Grammar: agreement, tense, articles and prepositions
skills.description: Choosing the grammatically correct sentence among close variants.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a verb agrees with its subject and that tense, article and preposition choices follow rules.
levels.GUIDED: Finds the error in a sentence with a checklist (subject, verb, tense, article, preposition).
levels.INDEPENDENT: Chooses the correct sentence among close variants unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Explains why each wrong variant is wrong — agreement with the nearest noun, tense sequence, "a" before a vowel sound, a fixed preposition.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, English Comprehension: "spot the error", "sentence improvement".
skills.expertCheck: Check each item against standard written English as taught in Indian classrooms, and that no variant marked wrong is accepted in Indian English usage.

skills.name: Sentence completion
skills.description: Filling a blank using the sentence's clue words, word forms and fixed expressions.

levels.AWARE: Knows that a blank is fixed by the sentence around it, including clue words such as although, despite and so … that.
levels.GUIDED: Uses the clue word to decide whether the blank continues or contrasts, with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Completes sentences with the right word and word form unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Catches a missed contrast signal, a confused word form or an unidiomatic pairing, and rereads the sentence with the choice in place.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, English Comprehension: "fill in the blanks".
skills.expertCheck: Check each blank has one best answer.

skills.name: Reading comprehension
skills.description: Main idea, detail, inference and word meaning from a short passage.

levels.AWARE: Knows the difference between a passage's main idea, a detail and an inference.
levels.GUIDED: Finds a stated detail and the main idea with guidance.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Answers main-idea, detail, inference and vocabulary-in-context questions unaided.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Rejects options that overstate the passage, bring in outside knowledge, change a detail or take a word literally, and points to the line that decides.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, English Comprehension: "comprehension passage"; UPSC GS Paper II "comprehension".
skills.expertCheck: The three passages are original and describe no real place or organisation; check they are neutral and at the right reading level.

skills.name: Idioms and phrases
skills.description: The meaning of common English idioms.

levels.AWARE: Knows that an idiom's meaning is not the sum of its words.
levels.GUIDED: Chooses the meaning of a common idiom from a sentence that uses it.
levels.INDEPENDENT: Chooses meanings of common idioms without a supporting sentence.
levels.TROUBLESHOOT: Rejects the literal reading and the opposite sense, and checks the meaning in a sentence of their own.

skills.basis: SSC CGL Tier-I, English Comprehension: "idioms and phrases".
skills.expertCheck: Check the idioms chosen are common in Indian English and the meanings match a standard dictionary.

misconceptions.title: Swaps HCF and LCM
misconceptions.description: Gives the highest common factor where the least common multiple is asked for, or the reverse.
misconceptions.basis: A common error for apt-q-number-properties (SSC CGL Tier-I, Quantitative Aptitude: "computation of whole numbers … relationships between numbers"; UPSC GS Paper II "basic numeracy (numbers and their relations)"; NCERT Class X, Real Numbers (HCF and LCM by prime factorisation).), described from standard teaching of the topic in the agent's own words; no source lists it verbatim.

items.prompt: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 18?

misconception.rationale: This is the other one of HCF and LCM.
This is the product of the numbers, which is a common multiple but not the least one when they share a factor.

items.explanation: The LCM is the smallest number both 12 and 18 divide into. 12 and 18 share the factor 6, so the LCM is 12 × 18 ÷ 6 = 36.
hints: You need a number that both numbers divide into — the smallest one.
Write each number as a product of primes, or list the multiples of the larger number until the smaller one divides it.
The multiples of 18 are 18, 36, 54, 72, …
Check which of the multiples of 18 is the first that 12 divides exactly.

items.prompt: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 36 and 48?

misconception.rationale: This is the other one of HCF and LCM.
This divides both numbers but is not the highest such number.

items.explanation: The HCF is the largest number that divides both. 36 = 12 × 3 and 48 = 12 × 4, and 3 and 4 share no factor, so the HCF is 12.
hints: You need the largest number that divides both numbers exactly.
Write both numbers as products of primes and multiply the primes they share.
6 divides both 36 and 48. Is there a larger number that also does?
Divide both numbers by 6: you get 6 and 8. If these still share a factor, multiply it into 6.

hints: Each light flashes at multiples of its own interval. When are all three at a multiple at once?
Find the least common multiple of the three intervals.
The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12. Now include 10.
Find the smallest multiple of 12 that 10 also divides.
